title: The zoom group matches the other tool bar groups, and double clicking the number goes to full size
goal: The zoom group sits at a different height from the tool groups beside it, so the row along the bottom of the canvas does not line up. Give it the same height. And double clicking the zoom percentage should take the picture to full size, which is what a person reaches for when they want to get back to a hundred percent.
notes: Reported by the user on 2026-09-07. The heights are hand written per group and they differ: the zoom bar uses vertical padding of 10 with horizontal 14 (EditorView.swift lines 1459 and following, around line 1496), the tool bar uses vertical 10 with horizontal 18 (line 737), and several other groups use vertical 8 (lines 437, 494, 564). So the row cannot line up, and the fix is to put the value in EditorChromeLayout beside the other chrome numbers and have every group read it, rather than correcting the zoom bar alone. Note the content inside a group can also set the height: the zoom bar holds a Slider and a Menu whose intrinsic heights may exceed the padding, so check the measured height rather than assuming the padding decides it. For the double click: the zoom readout is the label of a Menu (line 1475 onwards), and a Menu swallows clicks, so a double click gesture on the label alone will not arrive; the runner needs to handle that deliberately, for example a separate hit area or a gesture that recognises before the menu, and must keep the single click opening the menu.
acceptance: Every group along the bottom of the canvas is the same height and sits on the same centre line, measured rather than eyeballed, with the numbers in the audit
The heights come from one shared value rather than each group carrying its own, so a future group cannot drift again
Double clicking the zoom percentage sets the zoom to a hundred percent, and a single click still opens the zoom menu as it does now
Getting back to full size this way is one step that undo treats as one step, and the picture stays centred on what was on screen
The groups still line up at a narrow window, where some of them drop controls
Audit written under queue/audits/ with the bottom row at a wide and a narrow width, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: reviewed before building: the mock is not involved, this is the user's own report. The one thing the ask hides is a real collision — a menu opens on the press and owns every event until it closes, so the second click of a double click lands inside the menu. Either the menu waits a moment or the double click cannot exist. Chose the wait, capped at a quarter of a second (EditorChromeLayout.zoomReadoutDoubleClickWindow), and said so in the audit for the user to react to.

measured first, with a new probe rather than by eye: ToolBarLayoutProbe plus a `toolBar` playtest step report every group's frame. Before: Tools 48pt, Color 45pt, Zoom 35pt, all centre 800. Reproduced the complaint exactly.

one height for the row: EditorChromeLayout.toolBarGroupHeight (48, and toolBarHeight now reads from it). Every group swapped its own vertical padding for .frame(height:). After: 48pt on one centre line in wide, narrow, grid on, shape tool, wand, text, crop and adjust-grid states.

double click: ZoomReadoutClickLid, a transparent AppKit lid over the readout that takes clicks only (hover, highlight and tooltip fall through to the menu button underneath). One click opens the same SwiftUI menu after the wait; two go to actual size. Verified in a walk: 156% -> 100% with the view centre unchanged and undo untouched; a real click opens the menu with all ten rows; picking 400% still works; and it all holds in a narrow window where the capsule is only the number.
the lid also answers a click in an unfocused window (acceptsFirstMouse), which a tool bar should: without it the first click is spent activating the window and the number does nothing.
harness: `toolBar` step, `panelMenu` gained `clicking` so a walk can open a menu with a real click, and describe() now reports displayZoom and the document point in the middle of the window.
shared code, not a Next fork: EditorView is shared by both releases and both want a row that lines up, so per Releases/README the file stays shared and Current gets the fix too.

Every group along the bottom of the canvas is 48pt on one centre line, from EditorChromeLayout.toolBarGroupHeight; double clicking the zoom percentage goes to actual size while a single click still opens the stop menu. Measured in the running app with a new toolBar playtest step (before: 48/45/35pt; after: 48pt everywhere, wide and narrow, in eight tool states) and verified in three walks. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-07-toolbar-row.json. Committed as afe0fb8f.
